after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Given that $n\ge 2$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(n-2)!}{n!}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
n!=n\cdot (n-1)\cdot (n-2)!
$$

Then, we cancel the $(n-2)!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(n-2)!}{n!} & =\frac{(n-2)!}{n\cdot (n-1)\cdot (n-2)!} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(n-2)!}}{n\cdot (n-1)\cdot \cancel{(n-2)!}} \\  & =\frac{1}{n(n-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Given that $k\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{{k}^{2}(k-1)!}{(k+1)k!}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we notice that

$$
k!=k(k-1)!
$$

Then, we can cancel the $k(k-1)!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{k}^{2}(k-1)!}{(k+1)k!} & =\frac{k\cdot k(k-1)!}{(k+1)\cdot k(k-1)!} \\  & =\frac{k\cdot \cancel{k(k-1)!}}{(k+1)\cdot \cancel{k(k-1)!}} \\  & =\frac{k}{k+1}\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
First, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+1)! & =(m+1)\cdot m! \\ m! & =m\cdot (m-1)!\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can cancel the $m!$ and $(m-1)!$ that occur in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$

EXPLANATION

First, we notice that (m+5)!=(m+5)(m+4)!2m!=2m(2m−1)!

Then, we can cancel the (m+4)! and (2m−1)! that occur in both the numerator and the denominator:

(2m)!(m+4)!(m+5)!(2m−1)!=(2m)⋅(2m−1)!⋅(m+4)!(m+5)⋅(m+4)!⋅(2m−1)!=(2m)⋅(2m−1)!⋅(m+4)!(m+5)⋅(m+4)!⋅(2m−1)!=2mm+5

content.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Variable Expression Containing a Quotient With Many Factorials
content.problem: Given that $m\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(2m)!\,(m+4)!}{(m+5)!\,(2m-1)!}.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}(m+5)! & =(m+5)(m+4)! \\ 2m! & =2m(2m-1)!\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we can cancel the $(m+4)!$ and $(2m-1)!$ that occur in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(2m)!\,(m+4)!}{(m+5)!\,(2m-1)!} & =\frac{(2m)\,\cdot (2m-1)!\cdot (m+4)!}{(m+5)\cdot (m+4)!\cdot (2m-1)!} \\  & =\frac{(2m)\,\cdot \cancel{(2m-1)!}\cdot \cancel{(m+4)!}}{(m+5)\cdot \cancel{(m+4)!}\cdot \cancel{(2m-1)!}} \\  & =\frac{2m}{m+5}\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Given that $n\ge 1$ is an integer, simplify $\frac{(n-1)!}{(n+2)!}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice the following:

$$
(n+2)!=(n+2)\cdot (n+1)\cdot n\cdot (n-1)!
$$

Then, we cancel the $(n-1)!$ that occurs in both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
